sets.title: Monarch Migration Plan
sets.titleEs: Plan para la migración de las mariposas monarca

learn.rule: An outline turns notes into a plan: one topic sentence, then three details that support it. Then you write the paragraph from the plan.
learn.ruleEs: Un esquema convierte las notas en un plan: una oración temática y tres detalles que la apoyan. Luego escribes el párrafo desde el plan.
learn.model: Monarch butterflies make an amazing trip every fall. They fly up to 3,000 miles to reach forests in Mexico.
learn.notice: The first sentence is the big idea. The second sentence uses one note as a detail.

items.prompt: Put the outline parts in the right order.
lines: Topic: Monarch butterflies make a long trip each fall.
Detail 1: They leave the cool north when autumn comes.
Detail 2: They fly as far as 3,000 miles.
Detail 3: They rest in the forests of central Mexico.
items.why: An outline starts with the topic sentence. Then the details follow in the order a reader needs them.
items.whyEs: Un esquema empieza con la oración temática. Luego los detalles siguen en el orden que necesita el lector.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best topic sentence for these notes?
items.text: Notes: orange and black wings; fly south in the fall; travel up to 3,000 miles; spend the winter in the forests of Mexico.

options.text: Monarch butterflies have orange and black wings.
Butterflies are insects.
Monarch butterflies fly a very long way each fall to spend the winter in Mexico.

items.why: A good topic sentence covers most of the notes. Choice A uses only one note, and choice B is too big and leaves out the trip.
items.whyEs: Una buena oración temática cubre casi todas las notas. La opción A usa solo una nota y la opción B es demasiado general y no menciona el viaje.

items.prompt: Check the notes that should become details in an outline about the monarch trip.
items.text: Topic sentence: Monarch butterflies make a long trip each fall.

options.text: Bees make honey in wax combs.
They use the sun to help them find their way south.
Many monarchs gather in the same forests in Mexico.
Some butterflies are blue and green.
They travel up to 3,000 miles each fall.

items.why: A detail has to support the topic sentence. The correct notes explain how or where monarchs travel. The other notes are about bees and other butterflies.
items.whyEs: Un detalle tiene que apoyar la oración temática. Las notas correctas explican cómo o adónde viajan las monarcas. Las otras notas tratan de abejas y de otras mariposas.

items.prompt: Use the note 'they fly up to 3,000 miles' to finish the topic sentence.
items.model: Topic sentence: Monarchs make a long trip to Mexico each fall.
items.why: The note says 3,000 miles, so the trip is long. A topic sentence must agree with the notes it comes from.
items.whyEs: La nota dice 3,000 millas, así que el viaje es largo. Una oración temática debe coincidir con las notas de las que sale.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best detail to follow this topic sentence?
items.text: Topic sentence: Monarch butterflies make a long trip each fall.

options.text: Butterflies are insects with six legs.
Monarchs fly south for as many as 3,000 miles to reach warm forests.
Many people like butterfly gardens.

items.why: A detail must explain the topic sentence. Choice B tells how long the trip is. Choices A and C are true but do not explain the trip.
items.whyEs: Un detalle debe explicar la oración temática. La opción B dice qué tan largo es el viaje. Las opciones A y C son verdaderas, pero no explican el viaje.

items.prompt: Which complete sentence turns these note words into a detail?
items.text: Notes: rest, oyamel fir trees, Mexico

options.text: Oyamel fir trees growing in Mexico.
Resting in oyamel fir trees in Mexico.
Monarchs rest in oyamel fir trees in Mexico.

items.why: Notes are short word groups. A detail sentence needs a who and a what happens. Only choice C names the monarchs and tells what they do.
items.whyEs: Las notas son grupos cortos de palabras. Una oración de detalle necesita quién y qué pasa. Solo la opción C nombra a las monarcas y dice lo que hacen.

write.prompt: Use the outline to write one paragraph of four to six sentences. Start with the topic sentence.
write.promptEs: Usa el esquema para escribir un párrafo de cuatro a seis oraciones. Empieza con la oración temática.
write.text: Topic: Sea turtles begin life on sandy beaches. Detail 1: The mother digs a hole in the sand and lays about 100 eggs. Detail 2: She covers the eggs and returns to the sea. Detail 3: About two months later, the baby turtles hatch and crawl to the water.
write.frame: Sea turtles begin life on sandy beaches. First, ___

label: I used details from the outline
Usé detalles del esquema
I used a signal word like first, then, or finally
Usé una palabra de señal como first, then o finally

write.model: Sea turtles begin life on sandy beaches. First, a mother turtle digs a hole in the sand and lays about 100 eggs. Then she covers the nest and returns to the sea. About two months later, the baby turtles hatch and crawl toward the water.

familyTalk.en: Pick a family event, such as a birthday. Say one big idea about it and three details you would put in an outline.
familyTalk.es: Escojan un evento familiar, como un cumpleaños. Digan una idea grande sobre él y tres detalles que pondrían en un esquema.

teacherTip.en: Model turning two notes into full detail sentences on the board before students try the pick and blanks items.
teacherTip.es: Modela en la pizarra cómo convertir dos notas en oraciones de detalle completas antes de que los estudiantes hagan los ejercicios de selección y de espacios.

learn.rule: Sort your notes before you write. The big idea becomes the topic sentence, and the best facts become three details.
learn.ruleEs: Ordena tus notas antes de escribir. La idea principal se convierte en la oración temática y los mejores datos en tres detalles.
learn.model: The Pony Express moved mail across the country faster than ever before. Riders changed horses every 10 to 15 miles so they could keep going quickly.
learn.notice: The first sentence is the big idea about speed. The second sentence is one note written as a full sentence.

items.prompt: Choose the topic sentence that fits all of these notes.
items.text: Notes: riders carried mail; St. Joseph, Missouri to Sacramento, California; about 10 days; stations with fresh horses; ended in 1861 when telegraph lines linked the coasts.

options.text: Horses are fast animals.
Pony Express riders delivered mail across the country in about ten days.
The Pony Express lasted only a short time.

items.why: The topic sentence should cover most of the notes. Choice A is too general, and choice C covers only the last note.
items.whyEs: La oración temática debe cubrir casi todas las notas. La opción A es demasiado general y la opción C cubre solo la última nota.

items.prompt: Put these outline parts in order, from the topic to the last detail.
lines: Topic: The Pony Express sped mail across the country.
Detail 1: Riders raced from Missouri to California.
Detail 2: They changed horses at stations along the trail.
Detail 3: The telegraph ended the service in 1861.
items.why: The topic sentence comes first. The details follow in the order the labels give, and the ending comes last.
items.whyEs: La oración temática va primero. Los detalles siguen el orden de las etiquetas y el final va al último.

items.prompt: Check the notes that belong under the topic 'The Pony Express moved mail quickly.'

options.text: The trail stretched about 1,900 miles from Missouri to California.
Cattle ranches covered large parts of Texas.
A letter could cross the country in about ten days.
Corn grows best in warm, sunny weather.
Stations along the trail gave riders fresh horses.

items.why: Each correct note shows how the mail traveled fast. The notes about cattle and corn are true but belong to other topics.
items.whyEs: Cada nota correcta muestra cómo viajaba rápido el correo. Las notas sobre el ganado y el maíz son verdaderas, pero pertenecen a otros temas.

items.prompt: Finish the topic sentence so it matches the notes.
parts: Topic sentence: The Pony Express was a
items.model: Topic sentence: The Pony Express was a fast way to send mail in 1860.
items.why: The notes say the mail crossed the country in about ten days, so fast is the word that fits. Slow would disagree with the notes.
items.whyEs: Las notas dicen que el correo cruzaba el país en unos diez días, así que fast es la palabra correcta. Slow no coincidiría con las notas.

items.prompt: Which detail best supports this topic sentence?
items.text: Topic sentence: The telegraph ended the Pony Express.

options.text: Pony Express horses were chosen for their strength and speed.
Letters today travel by truck, train, and airplane.
In October 1861, telegraph wires linked the East and West coasts, so messages no longer needed riders.

items.why: A supporting detail has to explain the topic sentence. Only choice C tells how the telegraph made riders unnecessary.
items.whyEs: Un detalle de apoyo tiene que explicar la oración temática. Solo la opción C dice cómo el telégrafo hizo innecesarios a los jinetes.

items.prompt: Which complete sentence uses the notes 'fresh horses, stations, every 10 to 15 miles'?

options.text: Fresh horses waiting at stations.
Stations every 10 to 15 miles for fresh horses.
Riders got fresh horses at stations placed every 10 to 15 miles.

items.why: A detail sentence needs a who and an action. Choices A and B are word groups from notes, but choice C says who did what.
items.whyEs: Una oración de detalle necesita quién y una acción. Las opciones A y B son grupos de palabras como en las notas, pero la opción C dice quién hizo qué.

write.prompt: Use the outline to write one paragraph of four to six sentences. Start with the topic sentence.
write.promptEs: Usa el esquema para escribir un párrafo de cuatro a seis oraciones. Empieza con la oración temática.
write.text: Topic: A library helps a whole community. Detail 1: People borrow books, movies, and games for free. Detail 2: Children and adults join classes and clubs. Detail 3: Anyone can use the computers to learn and search.
write.frame: A library helps a whole community. First, ___

label: I used details from the outline
Usé detalles del esquema
I used a signal word like first, next, or finally
Usé una palabra de señal como first, next o finally

write.model: A library helps a whole community. First, people borrow books, movies, and games for free. Next, children and adults join classes and clubs there. Finally, anyone can use the computers to learn new things.

familyTalk.en: Choose a place in your community, such as a park or market. Say the big idea about it and three details together.
familyTalk.es: Escojan un lugar de su comunidad, como un parque o un mercado. Digan juntos la idea principal sobre él y tres detalles.

teacherTip.en: Give pairs a mixed set of notes and have them sort the notes into 'topic' and 'details' before they number the details.
teacherTip.es: Da a las parejas un grupo de notas mezcladas y pide que las clasifiquen en 'tema' y 'detalles' antes de numerar los detalles.

learn.rule: Plan with an outline. The topic sentence says the main idea, and three details show it with facts or examples.
learn.ruleEs: Planifica con un esquema. La oración temática dice la idea principal y tres detalles la muestran con datos o ejemplos.
learn.model: Fractions help people measure and share food. A cook uses 1/2 cup of milk when a recipe needs half a cup.
learn.notice: The first sentence is a big idea. The second sentence gives one real example with a fraction.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence matches these notes best?
items.text: Notes: recipes use 1/2 cup and 1/4 teaspoon; doubling a recipe means multiplying each amount; measuring cups have fraction marks.

options.text: A teaspoon is smaller than a cup.
Math is taught in school.
Fractions are useful tools for cooks.

items.why: The topic sentence has to cover all three notes. Choice A is too small, and choice B is too big and does not mention cooking.
items.whyEs: La oración temática tiene que cubrir las tres notas. La opción A es demasiado pequeña y la B es demasiado general y no menciona la cocina.

items.prompt: Put the outline in order, starting with the topic.
lines: Detail 1: Recipes list amounts such as 1/2 cup.
Detail 2: Measuring cups have fraction marks.
Detail 3: Doubling a recipe means multiplying each amount by 2.
items.why: The topic sentence is the big idea, so it leads. Each numbered detail then backs it up.
items.whyEs: La oración temática es la idea principal, así que va primero. Cada detalle numerado la respalda.

items.prompt: Check the notes that belong under the topic 'Fractions help people cook.'

options.text: A recipe may ask for 3/4 cup of milk.
A soccer field is about 100 yards long.
A cook can halve a recipe by cutting each amount in half.
Many students ride bikes to school.
Measuring spoons include 1/2 teaspoon and 1/4 teaspoon.

items.why: Each correct note shows a fraction used in cooking. The soccer field and bike notes do not connect to cooking.
items.whyEs: Cada nota correcta muestra una fracción usada al cocinar. Las notas del campo de fútbol y de las bicicletas no se relacionan con cocinar.

items.prompt: Finish this detail from the outline.
parts: To double a recipe, a cook
items.model: To double a recipe, a cook multiplies each amount by 2.
items.why: Doubling means making twice as much, and multiplying by 2 does that. Dividing by 2 would make half as much.
items.whyEs: Duplicar significa hacer el doble, y multiplicar por 2 lo logra. Dividir entre 2 haría la mitad.

items.prompt: Which sentence is a supporting detail instead of a topic sentence?

options.text: Fractions help people cook.
A half cup is the same as two quarter cups.
Fractions are useful for many jobs.

items.why: A detail gives one specific fact or example. Choice B is specific and true. Choices A and C are big ideas that a paragraph could be built around.
items.whyEs: Un detalle da un dato o ejemplo específico. La opción B es específica y verdadera. Las opciones A y C son ideas grandes sobre las que se puede construir un párrafo.

items.prompt: Which complete sentence uses the notes 'double, 2/3 cup, 1 1/3 cups'?

options.text: Doubling 2/3 cup to get 1 1/3 cups.
Two thirds of a cup, doubled, to get 1 1/3 cups.
When you double 2/3 cup, you get 1 1/3 cups.

items.why: A sentence needs a who or what and a complete action. Choices A and B are note-style fragments, but choice C is a whole idea.
items.whyEs: Una oración necesita un sujeto y una acción completa. Las opciones A y B son fragmentos como notas, pero la opción C es una idea completa.

write.prompt: Use the outline to write one paragraph of four to six sentences. Start with the topic sentence.
write.promptEs: Usa el esquema para escribir un párrafo de cuatro a seis oraciones. Empieza con la oración temática.
write.text: Topic: Walking to school has many benefits. Detail 1: It gives your body exercise. Detail 2: You can notice things in your neighborhood. Detail 3: Fewer cars on the road helps the air stay cleaner.
write.frame: Walking to school has many benefits. First, ___

label: I wrote about walking to school
Escribí sobre caminar a la escuela
I used details from the outline
Usé detalles del esquema
I used a signal word like first, next, or also
Usé una palabra de señal como first, next o also

write.model: Walking to school has many benefits. First, it gives your body healthy exercise before class. Next, you can notice birds, trees, and shops in your neighborhood. Also, fewer cars on the road helps keep the air cleaner.

familyTalk.en: While cooking, name one fraction in a recipe. Say a big idea about fractions and two details together.
familyTalk.es: Mientras cocinan, nombren una fracción de una receta. Digan juntos una idea grande sobre las fracciones y dos detalles.

teacherTip.en: Use real recipe cards or a measuring cup so students see the fractions before they sort the notes.
teacherTip.es: Usa tarjetas de recetas reales o una taza de medir para que los estudiantes vean las fracciones antes de clasificar las notas.
